append.text: **Ps 18:9 *præcéptum Dómini lúcidum* → *o decreto do Senhor é luminoso*** — the list's third place, held; passed every reader.

**Ps 18 has all three in eleven verses:** verbum 18:3 (*a palavra*), 18:5 (*as palavras deles*); sermónes 18:4 (*nem palavras*); elóquia 18:15a. Draft 1 kept elóquia apart as D26's clause (*E há de agradar o que disser a minha boca*): **the Latinist marked it MAJOR** (a future act of saying the Latin lacks; *erunt ut compláceant* flattened) and the stylist named it the psalm's worst line; draft 2 took his line, *E as palavras da minha boca serão tais que agradem* — outside Ps 118 elóquia is *palavras* (11:7, 17:31, D27), so the psalm follows them and the three Latin words meet in one Portuguese word here. Passed three gates.

Ps 18:10 *pérmanens in sǽculum sǽculi* → *permanece pelos séculos dos séculos*: the Latinist asked four times (minor) for *pelo século do século*, the stylist once for a cadence change — both refused (D27).
Ps 18:12 *in custodiéndis illis retribútio multa* → *em guardá-los há muita retribuição*; the blind reader heard a reward from God first, the fruit of keeping second — both in the Latin.

**Ps 18:6a *In sole pósuit tabernáculum suum* → *No sol pôs a sua tenda*** — the Latin's reading (the tent *in* the sun; the Hebrew's is *for* the sun); passed every reader; *tabernáculo* (MS1932) the option.
Ps 18:12 *custódit ea, in custodiéndis illis* → *os guarda, em guardá-los*; the blind reader heard 'obeys' first.

**Ps 18:13 *et ab aliénis parce servo tuo* → *e dos alheios poupai o vosso servo*** — three drafts: *das estranhas* (draft 1, the faults of others with *faltas* understood) failed three readers at once (Latinist MAJOR, the stylist, the blind reader, all hearing 'odd faults'); *das alheias* (draft 2) failed the gate MAJOR because **18:14b's masculine *domináti* makes its subject persons** (delícta would give *domináta*); *dos estranhos* (draft 3, persons) failed the gate MAJOR for closing out others' faults. *dos alheios* (the Latinist's fix twice) holds both, as the masculine/neuter *aliénis* does, and passed. So: *estranho* for persons named as such (17:46 *filhos estranhos*); a bare substantival *aliéni* may want *os alheios*.

**Ps 18:15b *Dómine, adjútor meus, et redémptor meus* → *Senhor, meu auxílio, e meu redentor* — HELD against four Latinist MAJORS (drafts 1–4), each asking *meu auxiliador*:** here the agent noun *redentor* stands beside it and the metonymy is most exposed (77:35 has the same pair, *Deus adjútor est eórum: et Deus excélsus redémptor eórum est*). Held for D19 and the psalter's one word; **needs a ruling** — proposal: keep *auxílio* in the formula places (*O Senhor é o meu auxílio*) but allow *auxiliador* where adjútor is paired with another agent noun (18:15b, 77:35), or settle *auxílio* everywhere and record the gate's objection as D24 does.
Ps 18:6b *Exsultávit ut gigas* → *Exultou como um gigante*: the blind reader listed *Exultou* as unknown (kept).

Ps 18:2 *Cæli enárrant … ópera mánuum ejus* → *Os céus narram … as obras das suas mãos*: the compound enarráre on the simple verb (one Greek verb, διηγοῦνται); the stylist named 18:2 the psalm's best line. See the new row enarráre.
Ps 18:15a *meditátio cordis mei* → *a meditação do meu coração*, the Latin's verbless second colon kept.
**Ps 18:8 *Lex Dómini immaculáta*, 18:14b *tunc immaculátus ero* → *imaculada / imaculado*** — the two places this row named; passed every reader.
Ps 18:12 *Étenim servus tuus* → *Pois o vosso servo*.
Ps 18:13 *Delícta quis intéllegit?* → *Quem entende as faltas?*

**Ps 18:8 *convértens ánimas* → *converte as almas*** — D25's exception again (the sense is conversion; DRB *converting*, MS1932 *converte*); the blind reader heard religious conversion first, as meant; *faz voltar as almas* is the option.
**Ps 18:3 *nox nocti índicat sciéntiam* → *uma noite indica o saber à outra noite*** — the place this row named; passed every reader; *o conhecimento* the option.

**Ps 18:13, 18:14b → *falta* three times** (*Quem entende as faltas? † Das minhas faltas ocultas purificai-me … da maior falta*): the noun supplied once for *ab occúltis meis*. The blind reader heard *faltas* as sins first ('absences' only third). Passed every gate.
Ps 18:5 *in fines orbis terræ* → *até os confins do mundo* (= Rom 10:18, checked in consult/bolls-VULG-45-10.json).

**Ps 18:3 *Dies diéi erúctat verbum* → *Um dia faz jorrar a palavra ao outro dia*** — the row's verb held in the second of its five places; no reader objected to the verb (the stylist's and the blind reader's trouble was the order of *O dia ao dia*, changed).
Ps 18:9 *illúminans óculos* → *ilumina os olhos*, beside *luminoso* for lúcidum (the pair); heard as 'gives understanding'.
Ps 18:8 *sapiéntiam præstans párvulis* → *dá sabedoria aos pequeninos*; heard as children, with the humble as second reading.

**Ps 18:9 *Justítiæ Dómini rectæ* → *As justiças do Senhor são retas*** — the Latin's plural kept though the Greek here is δικαιώματα (not δικαιοσύνας as at 10:8); heard as 'the acts by which the Lord does justice', norms second. Passed every reader.
**Ps 18:5 *in fines orbis terræ* → *até os confins do mundo*** — D30 held at the verse St Paul quotes (Rom 10:18, word for word in the Vulgate; τῆς οἰκουμένης).
Ps 18:9 *lætificántes corda* → *alegram os corações*.
Ps 18:10 *Timor Dómini sanctus* → *O temor do Senhor é santo*; heard as fear first, reverence second.

terms: | firmaméntum (the sky) | firmamento (*e o firmamento anuncia as obras das suas mãos*) | working (D31) | Ps 18:2 — D31's own example; στερέωμα, the vault. The blind reader listed *firmamento* as unknown (kept: D31, and the Latin's word). Other sky places (grep before use): 150:1 *in firmaménto virtútis ejus* |

| enarráre | narrar (*Os céus narram a glória de Deus*) | open | Ps 18:2; 49:16 *Quare tu enárras justítias meas* (grep: two places). On the simple verb (narráre → narrar); one Greek verb (διηγεῖσθαι) for both. MS1932 *publicam*; *proclamar* is prædicáre's |

| loquéla | linguagem (*Não há linguagens nem palavras*) | open | Ps 18:4 only (grep). λαλιαί; L&S 'speech, language, words, discourse'. A second word needed because sermo → palavra (D15) stands beside it. DRB *speeches*, MS1932 *linguagem*; *falas* the option. No reader remarked |

| thálamus | quarto nupcial (*como um esposo que sai do seu quarto nupcial*) | open | Ps 18:6a only (grep). Draft 1 *tálamo* (MS1932, the Diurnal): the stylist found it specialised and a proparoxytone at the cadence, the blind reader did not know it — the plainer of two faithful words taken. *câmara nupcial* (DRB) the option |

| gigas | gigante (*Exultou como um gigante para correr o caminho*) | open | Ps 18:6b; 32:16 *nec gigas salvábitur* (grep). The Latin's and the Greek's word (γίγας); the Hebrew's 'strong man' (the Diurnal *atleta*) not imported |

| summus (end of the sky) | extremo (*a sua saída é do extremo do céu … até o seu extremo*) | open | Ps 18:6b, 18:7b — the Latin repeats it (ἀπ᾿ ἄκρου … ἕως ἄκρου); one word twice. *alto* the option; *cimo* heard as a mountain's. Elsewhere (grep): 71:16 *in summis móntium* (the tops of the mountains — *cimo* fits there), 73:5 *super summum* |

| occúrsus | chegada (*E a sua chegada é até o seu extremo*) | open | Ps 18:7b only. L&S 'a meeting, falling in with'; the Greek κατάντημα is the arrival, the pair of ἔξοδος / egréssio (*saída*) in the line before. DRB *circuit*, MS1932 *curso* follow the Hebrew; *percurso* the option. Passed three gates |
| lúcidus | luminoso (*o decreto do Senhor é luminoso*) | open | Ps 18:9 (τηλαυγής), beside *ilumina*; DRB *lightsome*; *claro* the option (heard also as 'easy to understand') |

| desiderabílis + super | mais desejável que (*Mais desejáveis que o ouro e que muitas pedras preciosas*) | open | Ps 18:11 — *super* with the positive is the comparative, as the next colon's *dulcióra super* → *mais doces que*; the Latin's verbless line kept. Collective *lápidem pretiósum multum* → *muitas pedras preciosas* (the stylist; the Latinist asked three times, minor, for the singular — refused as number, D2), multus kept in both 18:11 and 18:12 (*muita retribuição*) |
| favus | favo (*mais doces que o mel e o favo*) | working | Ps 18:11 only (grep) |
| párcere | poupar (*poupai o vosso servo*) | open | Ps 18:13; 71:13 *Parcet páuperi et ínopi* (grep: two places). φείδομαι. *poupai* is safe at the *vós* imperative (past *poupei*) |

| mundáre / emundáre | purificar (*Das minhas faltas ocultas purificai-me … serei purificado da maior falta*) | open | Ps 18:13, 18:14b; 50:4 *a peccáto meo munda me*, 50:9 *et mundábor*, 88:45 *ab emundatióne* (grep; the adjective mundus 23:4, 50:12 → *puro*). καθαρίζω both. **Collision to watch:** 11:7 *purgátum* is already *purificada* (one line, another Greek word); if Ps 50 needs the two apart, *limpar* is the option for mundáre (DRB *cleanse*) |

| dominári (+ gen.) | dominar (*Se não me tiverem dominado*) | open | Ps 18:14b *Si mei non fúerint domináti*: **the Latinist marked the simple *dominarem* MAJOR** (the future perfect's anteriority) — the compound future subjunctive taken. The masculine *domináti* decides 18:13's *aliénis* (see aliénus) |

| redémptor | redentor (*e meu redentor*) | working | Ps 18:15b; 77:35 (grep: two places, both beside adjútor). λυτρωτής; the verb redímere → resgatar is its own row; the noun keeps the Christian word |

| complacére (*erunt ut compláceant*) | agradar (*serão tais que agradem*) | open | Ps 18:15a, the Latinist's fix (MAJOR on draft 1's *há de agradar*); ἔσονται εἰς εὐδοκίαν. The stylist's *serão do vosso agrado* the option (supplies *vosso*) |
formulas: | *In omnem terram exívit sonus eórum: * et in fines orbis terræ verba eórum* (18:5 = Rom 10:18) | *O som deles saiu por toda a terra: * e as palavras deles, até os confins do mundo* | working — Ps 18; the apostle's quotation, word for word in the Vulgate (consult/bolls-VULG-45-10.json); keep it identical wherever the Office quotes the verse |

| *Dómine, adjútor meus, et redémptor meus* (18:15b; 77:35 the pair in the third person) | *Senhor, meu auxílio, e meu redentor* | open — hangs on adjútor (held against four Latinist majors; for a ruling) |
